topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the opening framing, welcome, and key learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutational origins, and epidemiological patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer development, examining endogenous mutations, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological trends.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and mechanisms of infection-driven cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens drive oncogenesis, highlighting viral and bacterial mechanisms and the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific environmental mutagens, their metabolic activation pathways, and the molecular mechanisms by which they damage DNA.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanistic summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutational tumor promotion, host developmental susceptibilities, and summarize the diverse cellular mechanisms driving carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for detecting and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the experimental, epidemiological, and genomic methodologies used to evaluate carcinogens and weigh exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing framing and final summary remarks for the lecture.
